title: Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro
description: A 10.5 cm bronze statuette of a young woman, cast by the lost-wax method — one of the earliest known bronze sculptures in the world.
significance: Evidence of the astonishing metallurgical and artistic skill of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

title: Lion Capital of Ashoka
description: The polished sandstone capital of four addorsed lions that once topped an Ashokan pillar; adopted as India's State Emblem.
significance: A masterpiece of Mauryan art and the national emblem of the Republic of India.

title: Mithila Painting Panel
description: A hand-painted Mithila panel filled edge-to-edge with deities, fish and floral motifs in natural pigment.
significance: Represents a folk tradition carried by rural women for over two millennia.

title: Bagh Phulkari Shawl
description: A wedding shawl embroidered so densely with silk floss that the cotton base disappears entirely.
significance: An heirloom textile documenting Punjabi women's artistry and family life.

title: Jaipur Blue Pottery Vase
description: A clay-free quartz vase glazed in cobalt and turquoise with Persian floral motifs.
significance: A living record of Indo-Persian ceramic exchange.

title: Nataraja Bronze
description: A bronze of Shiva as Lord of the Dance within a ring of flames, the cosmos in balance on one foot.
significance: A pinnacle of Chola bronze casting and one of India's most recognised icons.

title: Terracotta Votive Horses
description: Hand-moulded terracotta horses offered at village shrines to local guardian deities.
significance: Reflects folk religion and the unbroken village pottery tradition.

title: Pattachitra Scroll
description: A cloth-based scroll painting of mythological scenes in natural colour with fine detailing.
significance: A narrative painting tradition tied to temple ritual and storytelling.
